summary: Every AI feature in the Counsel spec (legal agent_jobs plus agent actions on screens), with the gate it produces and its mock fixture. Real models are opt-in only (model.mode=live); dev, CI and e2e run against test/fakes/llm or the in-process fake.
sources: spec/legal/*.json agent_jobs and screen actions with by=agent

rules.rule: No test, dev run, CI job or e2e suite reaches a real model. model.mode defaults to mock; live needs model.mode=live plus an API key from the vault, and is refused when COUNSEL_ENV is test or ci.
rules.test: CI runs with egress to known model hosts denied and no key set; a ModelClient built with mode=live under COUNSEL_ENV=ci fails at boot with live_model_forbidden.

rules.rule: Every AI feature has a fixture directory testdata/ai/<feature>/ with at least ok, error_429, timeout and injection variants; a feature id without a fixture fails make check.
rules.test: tools/ai_fixture_lint.py: delete one fixture dir -> make check fails naming the feature id.

rules.rule: Model output never decides a gate. Each feature writes only draft/proposed rows or opens a gate through a2 write tools; the agent principal is never a decider.
rules.test: Per-feature acceptance asserts gate pending and agent decide -> 403 (ARC-I-016, ARC-I-035).

rules.rule: Fixtures and recorded prompts hold synthetic data only; no real client text, names or matter content are committed. Live recording is a manual, opt-in tool that writes to a scratch dir and requires review before commit.
rules.test: Fixture lint rejects files without the synthetic: true header.

rules.rule: Model calls are keyed and logged by feature id, token usage and cost only; prompt and completion text never reach Postgres or logs.
rules.test: Run a mock feature; grep the DB and slog output for the fixture completion text -> no match.
